def: The elected body that represents employees in a French company with at least eleven employees, and that the employer must inform and consult.

formal.ex: The [[Social and Economic Committee]] was informed and consulted on the proposed reorganisation at its meeting of 14 March.
formal.ex_us: The [[Social and Economic Committee]] was informed and consulted on the proposed reorganization at its meeting of March 14.

everyday.ex: We can't announce anything until we've been to the [[works council]].

collocations: to sit on the works council
note_fr: « Works council » est l'équivalent fonctionnel le mieux compris, mais rien d'identique n'existe au Royaume-Uni ni aux États-Unis, où la représentation passe d'abord par les syndicats. Évitez « enterprise committee » et « company committee ». À la première mention, donnez le sigle CSE suivi d'une glose.

explain.written: The CSE (comité social et économique, or Social and Economic Committee) is the elected employee representative body which French employers must set up once they have eleven employees and which must be informed and consulted on the running of the business.
explain.spoken: The CSE is our works council: employees elect it, and we have to consult it before any big decision about the organisation or people's jobs.

def: People chosen to speak and act for the workforce in dealings with the employer.

formal.ex: The Company shall provide [[employee representatives]] with the facilities they need to carry out their duties.

everyday.ex: The [[staff reps]] have asked for a meeting before the end of the week.
everyday.ex_us: The [[employee reps]] have asked for a meeting before the end of the week.

collocations: to act on behalf of the workforce
note_fr: « Personnel representatives » et « delegates of the personnel » sont des calques. « Personnel » vieillit en anglais : on dit « staff », « employees » ou « the workforce ». Aux États-Unis, « representative » fait d'abord penser au représentant syndical.

def: An employee who has been voted onto the works council by his or her colleagues.

formal.uk: elected member of the works council
formal.us: elected member of the works council
formal.ex: Each [[elected member of the works council]] receives training in economic matters at the start of the term.

everyday.ex: She's been a [[council member]] for six years and knows the site inside out.

collocations: to be elected to the works council
note_fr: « An elected » n'existe pas comme nom : dites « an elected member » ou « a council member ». Siéger : « to sit on the council », jamais « to seat ».

def: A person elected to take the place of a full member of the works council when that member is absent.

formal.ex: A [[substitute member]] shall attend meetings only in the absence of the full member whom he or she replaces.
formal.ex_us: An [[alternate member]] shall attend meetings only in the absence of the regular member whom he or she replaces.

everyday.ex: Paul can't make it on Thursday, so his [[substitute]] will sit in for him.
everyday.ex_us: Paul can't make it on Thursday, so his [[alternate]] will sit in for him.

collocations: to stand in for a full member
note_fr: Titulaire : « full member » (US : « regular member »). « Titular » est un faux ami : il signifie « en titre seulement », sans pouvoir réel. En droit français, le suppléant ne siège en principe qu'en l'absence du titulaire.

def: The elected member chosen by the works council to draw up the agenda with the employer and to write the minutes.

formal.ex: The agenda is drawn up jointly by the chair and the [[secretary of the works council]].

everyday.ex: I'd run it past the [[council secretary]] informally before the papers go out.

collocations: to draw up the agenda jointly
note_fr: Faux ami de fonction : ce « secretary » est un élu, interlocuteur principal de la direction, et non un(e) assistant(e). Précisez-le à un interlocuteur étranger, qui pourrait sous-estimer son rôle.

explain.written: The secretary of the works council is an elected employee member who agrees the agenda of each meeting with the employer and is responsible for the minutes.
explain.spoken: The council secretary is the elected member who speaks for the council day to day - we agree the agenda with them and they write the minutes.

def: To lead a meeting or a committee and keep its discussions in order.

formal.ex: The works council [[is chaired]] by the employer or by its duly authorised representative.
formal.ex_us: The works council [[is chaired]] by the employer or by its duly authorized representative.

everyday.ex: The site director [[runs the meeting]], but she can't set the agenda on her own.

collocations: the chair of the works council
note_fr: « To preside over » existe mais reste solennel. « The chair » désigne la personne qui préside, terme neutre aujourd'hui préféré à « chairman ». Particularité à expliquer : en France, c'est l'employeur qui préside l'instance.

def: The period for which a person is elected to a position.

formal.ex: Members are elected for a [[term of office]] of four years, unless a collective agreement provides for a shorter term.

everyday.ex: He's coming to the end of his second [[term]] and isn't sure he'll stand again.
everyday.ex_us: He's coming to the end of his second [[term]] and isn't sure he'll run again.

collocations: to be re-elected for a further term
note_fr: « Mandate » désigne en anglais la légitimité ou la mission confiée (« a mandate to negotiate »), pas la durée des fonctions. « During his mandate » est un calque : dites « during his term ».

def: To put oneself forward as a candidate so that people can vote for you.

formal.ex: Any employee with at least one year's service may [[stand as a candidate]].
formal.ex_us: Any employee with at least one year of service may [[run as a candidate]].

everyday.ex: Are you going to [[stand]] again next year?
everyday.ex_us: Are you going to [[run]] again next year?

note_fr: « To present oneself to the elections » est un calque. Différence nette : on « stands » au Royaume-Uni, on « runs » aux États-Unis. Candidat sortant : « the sitting member » (UK), « the incumbent » (US).

def: The elections in which employees of a French company choose the members of the works council.

formal.ex: The employer must organise [[elections of employee representatives]] once the workforce threshold has been reached.
formal.ex_us: The employer must organize [[elections of employee representatives]] once the workforce threshold has been reached.

everyday.ex: The [[works council elections]] are in March, so the unions are already campaigning.

collocations: to draw up the electoral roll
note_fr: « Professional elections » ne veut rien dire en anglais (« professional » renvoie à un métier qualifié). Aux États-Unis, « union election » désigne tout autre chose : le vote par lequel les salariés décident d'être ou non représentés par un syndicat.

explain.written: Workplace elections (élections professionnelles) are the ballots, held in principle every four years, in which the employees of a French company elect the members of the works council and which also determine which unions have representative status.
explain.spoken: Every four years or so, staff vote for their works council members - and the results also decide which unions get a seat at the negotiating table.

def: An agreement negotiated between the employer and the unions before workplace elections, fixing how the vote will be organised.

formal.ex: The [[pre-election agreement]] determines the allocation of seats between the electoral colleges and the arrangements for voting.

everyday.ex: We need to invite the unions to negotiate the [[pre-election agreement]] before we fix a date.

collocations: to invite the unions to negotiate
note_fr: « Protocol » évoque en anglais l'étiquette ou une procédure technique ; pour un accord, dites « agreement ». Gardez le sigle PAP uniquement entre spécialistes du droit français.

explain.written: The pre-election agreement (protocole d'accord préélectoral) is negotiated between the employer and the unions ahead of workplace elections and lays down the practical arrangements for the ballot, including the allocation of seats.
explain.spoken: Before the elections, we sit down with the unions and agree the ground rules: how many seats, who votes where, and when.

def: A group of voters, defined by job category, who elect their own representatives separately from other groups.

formal.ex: Employees vote in separate [[electoral colleges]] according to their occupational category.

everyday.ex: Managers and engineers are in a separate [[voting group]] from the shop floor.

note_fr: Pour un Américain, « the Electoral College » évoque l'élection présidentielle : précisez « for works council elections ». Cadres : « managerial and professional staff » ; ouvriers et employés : « manual and clerical staff ».

explain.written: For workplace elections, French employees are divided into electoral colleges (collèges électoraux) by occupational category, each of which elects its own representatives.
explain.spoken: People don't all vote together: manual and clerical staff vote in one group, supervisors and managers in another, and each group elects its own reps.

def: A vote in which nobody can see how each person has voted.

formal.ex: Members of the works council are elected by [[secret ballot]].

everyday.ex: If it's about a named person, we hold a [[secret ballot]] rather than a show of hands.

note_fr: « Ballot » désigne à la fois le scrutin et le bulletin (« ballot paper » au Royaume-Uni). « Bulletin » est un faux ami : il signifie communiqué ou lettre d'information. Voter à main levée : « by a show of hands ».

def: A further vote held when the first one has not produced a valid result.

formal.ex: If the quorum is not reached, a [[second round of voting]] is held within fifteen days, in which non-union candidates may stand.
formal.ex_us: If the quorum is not reached, a [[second round of voting]] is held within fifteen days, in which non-union candidates may run.

everyday.ex: Turnout was too low, so it's going to a [[second round]].
everyday.ex_us: Turnout was too low, so it's going to a [[runoff]].

collocations: to go to a second round
note_fr: « Tour » ne se traduit pas par « tour » (= visite, tournée) ni par « turn ». Particularité française à expliquer : au premier tour, seules les organisations syndicales peuvent présenter des listes.

def: Paid working hours that employee or union representatives may spend on their representative role instead of their job.

formal.uk: paid time off for representative duties
formal.ex: Each full member is entitled to [[paid time off for representative duties]], which is treated as working time.
formal.ex_us: Each regular member is entitled to [[paid release time]], which is treated as working time.

everyday.ex: He's on [[facility time]] this afternoon, so he won't be at his desk.
everyday.ex_us: He's on [[release time]] this afternoon, so he won't be at his desk.

collocations: to take time off for union duties
note_fr: « Delegation hours » est incompréhensible. Au Royaume-Uni, « facility time » vise surtout les représentants syndicaux ; aux États-Unis, « release time » (« official time » dans le secteur public fédéral) se négocie dans l'accord collectif au lieu d'être fixé par la loi.

explain.written: Heures de délégation are the monthly allowance of paid hours which French law grants employee and union representatives to carry out their duties, and which count as working time.
explain.spoken: Reps get a set number of paid hours a month for their council or union work - they just tell their manager they're off, they don't need permission.

def: An employee, typically a staff or union representative, who has special legal protection against dismissal.

formal.ex: As a [[protected employee]], he may not be dismissed without the prior authorisation of the labour inspector.
formal.ex_us: As a [[protected employee]], he may not be dismissed without the prior authorization of the labor inspector.

everyday.ex: She's got [[protected status]] as a works council member, so the usual procedure doesn't apply.
everyday.ex_us: She has [[protected status]] as a works council member, so the usual procedure doesn't apply.

collocations: protection continues after the term ends
note_fr: Aux États-Unis, « protected » renvoie plutôt aux « protected classes » (discrimination) ou à la « protected concerted activity ». Au Royaume-Uni, licencier quelqu'un pour ses activités syndicales est « automatically unfair », mais aucune autorisation administrative n'est requise.

explain.written: A protected employee (salarié protégé) is an employee, such as a works council member or union delegate, whose dismissal or transfer requires the prior authorisation of the labour inspector.
explain.spoken: Reps have protected status in France: we can't dismiss them unless the labour inspector, who's a public official, signs it off first.

def: The official permission an employer must obtain from the French labour inspectorate before dismissing a protected employee.

formal.uk: prior authorisation of the labour inspector
formal.us: prior authorization of the labor inspector
formal.ex: The dismissal of a staff representative requires the [[prior authorisation of the labour inspector]].
formal.ex_us: The dismissal of a staff representative requires the [[prior authorization of the labor inspector]].

everyday.ex: We can't do anything until we get [[sign-off from the labour inspector]], and that can take a couple of months.
everyday.ex_us: We can't do anything until we get [[sign-off from the labor inspector]], and that can take a couple of months.

note_fr: Fonction sans équivalent exact : pas d'inspection du travail généraliste au Royaume-Uni, et aux États-Unis aucune autorité n'autorise un licenciement. L'idée surprend toujours : expliquez-la d'emblée plutôt que de la supposer connue.

explain.written: Under French law, a protected employee may be dismissed only with the prior authorisation of the labour inspector, a public official who checks that the dismissal is justified and unconnected with the employee's representative duties.
explain.spoken: Before we can dismiss a rep, a government inspector has to check the case and give the go-ahead - without that, the dismissal is void.

def: The criminal offence committed by a French employer who prevents employee representative bodies from being set up or from working properly.

formal.uk: the offence of obstructing employee representative bodies
formal.us: the offense of obstructing employee representative bodies
formal.ex: Failure to consult the works council may constitute [[the offence of obstructing employee representative bodies]].
formal.ex_us: Failure to consult the works council may constitute [[the offense of obstructing employee representative bodies]].

everyday.ex: If we sign before the council has given its opinion, they'll go after us for [[obstruction]].

note_fr: Ne traduisez pas par « hindrance » ni « obstacle ». Insistez sur le caractère pénal (« it's a criminal offence »), qui surprend les Anglo-Saxons. L'analogie américaine la plus proche, très imparfaite, est l'« unfair labor practice », qui n'est pas pénale.

explain.written: The délit d'entrave is a criminal offence under French law, committed by an employer who interferes with the setting up, the free election or the proper functioning of employee representative bodies.
explain.spoken: If we skip the works council or keep information from it, that's not just a procedural slip in France - it's a criminal offence, and the manager in charge can be prosecuted.

def: The list of matters to be discussed at a meeting.

formal.ex: The [[agenda]] shall be sent to members at least three days before the meeting.

everyday.ex: Can we get the shift changes onto the [[agenda]] for next month?

collocations: to put an item on the agenda
note_fr: « Agenda » n'est jamais un carnet de rendez-vous (« diary » au Royaume-Uni, « planner » ou « calendar » aux États-Unis). « Order of the day » est un calque. Questions diverses : « any other business ».

def: The official written record of what was said and decided at a meeting.

formal.ex: The [[minutes of the meeting]] are drawn up by the secretary and submitted for approval at the following meeting.

everyday.ex: Who's taking the [[minutes]] today?

collocations: to record something in the minutes
note_fr: Toujours au pluriel ; « to minute something » = consigner au procès-verbal. « Process verbal » n'existe pas et « report » est trop vague. Prononciation /ˈmɪnɪts/, à ne pas confondre avec l'adjectif « minute » /maɪˈnjuːt/ (minuscule).

def: To ask the members of a meeting to decide a question by voting on it.

formal.uk: to put the resolution to the vote
formal.us: to put the resolution to a vote
formal.ex: The chair [[put the resolution to the vote]]; it was carried by eight votes to three, with one abstention.
formal.ex_us: The chair [[put the resolution to a vote]]; it was carried by eight votes to three, with one abstention.

everyday.ex: Shall we [[take a vote]], or does anyone need more time?

note_fr: Une voix = « a vote », jamais « a voice ». Une résolution est « carried » ou « passed » (adoptée), « defeated » (rejetée). À rappeler à un interlocuteur étranger : le président ne vote pas lorsqu'il consulte les élus en tant que délégation du personnel.

def: To arrange for people to come together for a formal meeting.

formal.ex: The employer shall [[convene a meeting]] of the works council at the intervals laid down by law or by agreement.

everyday.ex: Management has [[called a meeting]] for Tuesday to talk about the site closure.

collocations: to send out the notice of meeting
at the request of a majority of members
note_fr: « To convoke » est rarissime, et « convocation » désigne une cérémonie universitaire. « To summon » = convoquer d'autorité (tribunal, hiérarchie) : trop fort pour une réunion. La convocation écrite : « notice of meeting ».

def: The process by which an employer gives employee representatives the facts about a plan and asks for their views before deciding.

formal.ex: The project is subject to prior [[information and consultation]] of the works council.

everyday.ex: We have to [[inform and consult]] the council before the board takes its decision.

collocations: to inform and consult on a project
note_fr: « Information » est indénombrable : jamais « an information » ni « informations ». Au Royaume-Uni, l'expression évoque surtout la consultation collective sur les licenciements et les transferts ; aux États-Unis, l'employeur n'a aucune obligation générale de consulter.

def: To ask the works council formally for its views on a plan before the decision is taken.

formal.uk: to consult the works council on
formal.us: to consult the works council on
formal.ex: The Company is required to [[consult the works council on]] any measure likely to affect the size or structure of the workforce.

everyday.uk: to go to the works council
everyday.us: to go to the works council
everyday.ex: We'll need to [[go to the works council]] with this before we tell the managers.

note_fr: « Consult » se construit avec « on » ou « about » pour le sujet. « To consult with » (surtout US) implique un échange. Consulter n'est pas demander la permission : l'avis du CSE ne lie pas l'employeur, dites-le clairement à votre interlocuteur.

def: To state formally, as a body, what one thinks of a proposal after being consulted.

formal.ex: The works council shall [[deliver its opinion]] within the time limit set by agreement or, failing that, by regulation.

everyday.ex: The council won't [[give its opinion]] until the expert's report is in.

collocations: to be deemed to have been consulted
note_fr: On dit « opinion », pas « advice » (= conseil) ni « notice » (= préavis). L'avis est consultatif : « non-binding » ou « advisory ». Si le CSE ne se prononce pas dans le délai, il est réputé avoir rendu un avis négatif : « it is deemed to have given a negative opinion ».

def: A formal statement by a consulted body that it approves of a proposal (or, if unfavourable, that it does not).

formal.ex: The works council delivered a [[favourable opinion]] by nine votes to two.
formal.ex_us: The works council delivered a [[favorable opinion]] by nine votes to two.

everyday.uk: to come out in favour of
everyday.us: to come out in favor of
everyday.ex: The council [[came out in favour of]] the new shift pattern, with a few reservations.
everyday.ex_us: The council [[came out in favor of]] the new shift schedule, with a few reservations.

informal.ex: The reps [[gave the thumbs-up]] to the hybrid working policy.

collocations: by a majority of members present
note_fr: « Negative opinion » et « unfavourable opinion » se disent tous deux. Une personne « votes against » ; l'instance « comes out against ». Un avis défavorable ne bloque pas le projet : « the employer may still go ahead ».

def: The length of time employee representatives have to give their views on a proposal.

formal.ex: The [[time limit for consultation]] starts to run when the employer provides the required information.

everyday.ex: The [[consultation period]] runs out on the 30th, so the board can't meet before then.

note_fr: « Delay » signifie « retard », jamais « délai » : dites « time limit », « period » ou « deadline » (date butoir). Au Royaume-Uni, « consultation period » évoque d'abord la consultation collective préalable aux licenciements économiques.

fr: BDESE (base de données économiques, sociales et environnementales)
def: The set of company data that a French employer must make available to employee representatives for their regular consultations.

formal.ex: The information required for the recurring consultations is made available in the [[economic, social and environmental database]].

everyday.ex: The pay-gap figures are already in [[the works council database]], so the reps have had them for weeks.

collocations: to upload data to the database
to keep the database up to date
to have access to the database
note_fr: Gardez le sigle BDESE avec une glose à la première occurrence. « Database » s'écrit en un mot. « Data » prend un verbe au singulier dans l'usage courant (« the data is »), au pluriel dans un style soutenu.

explain.written: The BDESE (economic, social and environmental database) brings together the information on the company's finances, workforce and environmental impact which the employer must make available to the works council and union delegates.
explain.spoken: It's a shared database where we post the figures the reps are entitled to see: headcount, pay, investment, that sort of thing.

fr: recours à un expert (par le CSE)
def: For a works council, to decide to bring in an outside specialist, usually an accountant, to help it examine the employer's plans.

formal.ex: The works council resolved [[to appoint an expert]] to assist it in the consultation on the Company's financial position.

everyday.ex: The council has [[brought in an expert]], which buys them another month.

note_fr: « Expertise » en anglais = compétence, savoir-faire (indénombrable), jamais la mission ni le rapport : dites « expert's review » ou « expert's report ». Expert-comptable : « chartered accountant » (UK), « CPA » (US).

explain.written: In certain consultations the French works council may appoint an outside expert, usually an accounting firm, whose fees are borne wholly or mainly by the employer and whose appointment extends the consultation period.
explain.spoken: The council can bring in its own outside expert to go through our numbers - we pay for most of it, and it gives them extra time before they give their opinion.

def: The power of French employee representatives to raise a formal concern with the employer, who is then obliged to respond.

formal.ex: The works council exercised its economic [[right of alert]] and asked management to explain the fall in orders.

everyday.ex: The reps [[raised the alarm]] about workloads in the call centre months ago.
everyday.ex_us: The reps [[raised the alarm]] about workloads in the call center months ago.

note_fr: Plusieurs droits d'alerte coexistent (économique, danger grave et imminent, atteinte aux droits des personnes) : précisez lequel. Ne confondez pas avec « whistleblowing », qui est une démarche individuelle.

explain.written: The right of alert (droit d'alerte) allows the works council to raise a formal concern, for instance about the company's financial position or a serious and imminent danger, to which the employer is required to respond.
explain.spoken: If the reps think something is seriously wrong - the finances, or a safety risk - they can trigger a formal procedure, and we have to give them answers.

def: The leisure, holiday and welfare benefits that a French works council organises for employees with money provided by the employer.

formal.ex: The works council manages the [[social and cultural activities]] funded by the employer's annual contribution.

everyday.ex: Holiday vouchers and cinema tickets come out of the [[works council benefits]] budget, not ours.
everyday.ex_us: Vacation vouchers and movie tickets come out of the [[works council benefits]] budget, not ours.

note_fr: Aucun équivalent : dans les pays anglo-saxons, ces avantages relèvent de l'employeur (« employee benefits », « perks ») ou d'un « social committee » bénévole. « Social » seul évoque les loisirs entre collègues (« a staff social »).

explain.written: In France the works council itself manages a budget, funded by the employer, for social and cultural activities such as holiday vouchers, gift vouchers and subsidised leisure for employees and their families.
explain.spoken: The works council has its own budget for staff perks - holiday vouchers, Christmas gifts, cheap cinema tickets - and it decides how the money is spent, not us.

def: A body through which a multinational group informs and consults representatives of its employees in several European countries.

formal.ex: Transnational matters fall within the remit of the [[European Works Council]].

everyday.ex: The [[EWC]] meets once a year in Brussels, with interpreters.

note_fr: Depuis le Brexit, le Royaume-Uni ne relève plus du dispositif européen, mais vos interlocuteurs britanniques connaissent le terme. Aux États-Unis, glosez : « a body for informing and consulting employees across Europe ».

def: The number of employees above which a legal obligation starts to apply to a company.

formal.ex: Once the [[workforce threshold]] of fifty employees has been reached for twelve consecutive months, the works council acquires wider powers.

everyday.ex: We're about to cross the [[headcount threshold]], so we need to budget for a works council with full powers.

note_fr: « Effective » est un adjectif (efficace, effectif) : l'effectif se dit « headcount » ou « workforce ». « Threshold » ne prend qu'un seul « h » au milieu et se prononce /ˈθreʃhəʊld/.

def: In a French company with several establishments, the works council at company level, made up of delegates from the site councils.

formal.ex: Projects decided at company level which affect more than one establishment fall within the remit of the [[Central Social and Economic Committee]].

everyday.ex: It goes to the [[central works council]] first, then to the two sites affected.

collocations: to chair the central works council
to fall within the remit of
note_fr: Expliquez l'articulation : le CSE central est consulté sur les projets décidés au niveau de l'entreprise ; les CSE d'établissement le sont sur les mesures d'adaptation propres à leur site. « Remit » (UK) = champ de compétence ; aux États-Unis, dites plutôt « scope » ou « purview ».

explain.written: The central works council (CSE central) is the company-level body which, in a French company with several establishments, is informed and consulted on projects concerning the company as a whole; its members are drawn from the establishment-level works councils.
explain.spoken: We have a works council at each site, and above them a central one for the whole company - anything decided at company level goes to the central council first.

def: The works council elected at one establishment of a company that has several.

formal.ex: Each [[establishment-level works council]] is consulted on the measures adapting the project to its own site.

everyday.ex: The [[site works council]] in Nantes is a good deal tougher than the one in Lille.

collocations: the site director chairs the council
note_fr: « Establishment » est juridique et formel ; à l'oral, on dit « site » ou « location » (US). Attention : « the Establishment », avec majuscule, désigne les élites au pouvoir. Chef d'établissement : « site director » ou « site manager ».

def: In French law, a site or group of sites that is treated as a unit of its own for electing a works council.

formal.ex: The number and boundaries of [[separate establishments]] are fixed by company agreement or, failing that, by the employer, having regard to the autonomy of local management.

everyday.uk: to count as a separate site
everyday.us: to count as a separate site
everyday.ex: The depot doesn't [[count as a separate site]], because its manager has no real say over staffing.

collocations: the autonomy of the site manager
note_fr: « Périmètre » se rend par « scope » ou « boundaries » : « perimeter » ne désigne qu'une limite physique (clôture, enceinte). Le critère à expliquer est l'autonomie de gestion du responsable du site, notamment en matière de personnel.

explain.written: A separate establishment (établissement distinct) is a unit of the company, defined by agreement or, failing that, by the employer on the basis of the management autonomy of the person in charge, within which a works council of its own is elected.
explain.spoken: We have to decide how the company is carved up for representation: each 'separate establishment' gets its own works council, and the test is how much real autonomy the local manager has.

def: A group of legally separate French companies treated as a single company for the purposes of employee representation.

formal.ex: The three subsidiaries were recognised by agreement as forming an [[economic and social unit]], with a single works council.
formal.ex_us: The three subsidiaries were recognized by agreement as forming an [[economic and social unit]], with a single works council.

everyday.uk: to be treated as a single company
everyday.us: to be treated as a single company
everyday.ex: For representation purposes the three subsidiaries [[are treated as a single company]], even though they're separate legal entities.

collocations: to be recognised by agreement or by the court
note_fr: Notion sans équivalent : gardez le sigle UES avec une glose. Les analogies (« associated employers » au Royaume-Uni, « single employer » aux États-Unis) répondent à d'autres finalités : présentez-les comme de simples points de repère. Entité juridique : « legal entity », pas « juridical ».

explain.written: An economic and social unit (unité économique et sociale, or UES) is a group of legally distinct companies which, because they share common management, complementary activities and a single workforce community, are treated as one company for the purposes of employee representation.
explain.spoken: Legally they're three companies, but because they're run together and the staff work as one community, French law treats them as one for the works council and the unions.

def: An organisation of workers that defends its members' interests and negotiates with employers on their behalf.

formal.ex: Every employee is free to join the [[trade union]] of his or her choice.
formal.ex_us: Every employee is free to join the [[labor union]] of his or her choice.

everyday.ex: The [[union]] wants a meeting before we announce anything.

note_fr: « Syndicate » est un faux ami : consortium financier ou organisation criminelle. « Labour union » ne se dit guère au Royaume-Uni, où « Labour » évoque le parti. À l'oral, « the union » suffit.

def: To become a member of a union.

formal.uk: to become a member of a trade union
formal.us: to become a member of a labor union
formal.ex: No employee may be penalised for choosing to [[become a member of a trade union]].
formal.ex_us: No employee may be penalized for choosing to [[become a member of a labor union]].

everyday.ex: Half the warehouse staff decided to [[join a union]] after the restructuring was announced.

informal.ex: Most of the new drivers have [[signed up]] already.

note_fr: « To adhere to » = respecter (une règle), pas adhérer à une organisation. Un adhérent : « member », jamais « adherent » (adepte d'une doctrine). Pas de préposition : « to join a union », et non « to join to ».

def: A person who belongs to a union.

formal.ex: [[Union members]] may not be treated less favourably on account of their membership.
formal.ex_us: [[Union members]] may not be treated less favorably on account of their membership.

everyday.ex: The plant is heavily [[unionised]]; head office much less so.
everyday.ex_us: The plant is heavily [[unionized]]; corporate much less so.

note_fr: « Syndicated » = diffusé par plusieurs médias. Taux de syndicalisation : « union density ». Rappelez qu'en France les accords s'appliquent à tous les salariés, syndiqués ou non : d'où une faible adhésion mais une couverture conventionnelle très élevée.

def: A person appointed by a union to represent it in a company and to negotiate with the employer on its behalf.

formal.ex: Each representative union may appoint a [[union delegate]], who has authority to negotiate and sign company agreements on its behalf.

everyday.ex: I'd have a quiet word with the [[union rep]] before the meeting.

collocations: to negotiate on behalf of the union
note_fr: Ne confondez pas l'élu du CSE (élu par les salariés) et le délégué syndical (désigné par son syndicat) : au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis, le représentant syndical cumule les deux rôles. « Syndical delegate » est un calque.

explain.written: The union delegate (délégué syndical) is an employee appointed by a representative union, in companies with fifty or more employees, to represent it in dealings with the employer and to negotiate company agreements.
explain.spoken: The union delegate isn't elected by staff - the union appoints them, and they're the person we negotiate and sign agreements with.

def: An employee elected by fellow union members to represent them in day-to-day dealings with local management.

formal.ex: The [[workplace representative]] is entitled to accompany a member to a disciplinary hearing.
formal.ex_us: The [[union steward]] is entitled to be present at an investigatory interview that may lead to discipline.

everyday.ex: The [[shop steward]] on the night shift is pretty reasonable, to be fair.
everyday.ex_us: The [[steward]] on the night shift is pretty reasonable, to be fair.

collocations: to raise an issue with the steward
note_fr: Le « shop steward » est un salarié élu par ses collègues syndiqués pour les représenter sur le terrain : ni élu du CSE, ni tout à fait délégué syndical. « Shop » désigne ici l'atelier (« shop floor »), pas le magasin.

def: The local unit of a union, made up of its members in a particular workplace or area.

formal.ex: A union may set up a [[workplace union branch]] once it has several members in the company.
formal.ex_us: A union may establish a [[local union]] once it has several members in the company.

everyday.ex: The [[branch]] meets on the first Monday of the month.
everyday.ex_us: The [[local]] meets on the first Monday of the month.

note_fr: « Syndical section » ne dit rien à un anglophone. Aux États-Unis, « the local » est l'unité de base du syndicat, généralement désignée par un numéro. Tract : « leaflet » (UK), « flyer » (US) ; panneau syndical : « union noticeboard » (UK), « union bulletin board » (US).

def: The legal standing that allows a French union to appoint a delegate and to negotiate and sign collective agreements.

formal.ex: A union acquires [[representative status]] in the company if, among other criteria, it wins at least ten per cent of the votes cast in the first round.
formal.ex_us: A union acquires [[representative status]] in the company if, among other criteria, it wins at least ten percent of the votes cast in the first round.

everyday.ex: They only got eight per cent, so they no longer [[count as representative]] and lose their seat at the table.
everyday.ex_us: They only got eight percent, so they no longer [[count as representative]] and lose their seat at the table.

note_fr: « Representativity » est un calque ; « representativeness » existe mais reste abstrait : préférez « representative status ». Les équivalents fonctionnels sont « recognition » (UK) et « certification » (US), mais là-bas un seul syndicat représente en général l'unité de négociation.

explain.written: Representative status (représentativité) is the standing which a French union must have in order to negotiate and sign collective agreements; at company level it depends in particular on winning at least ten per cent of the votes in workplace elections.
explain.spoken: A union only gets to negotiate with us if it's 'representative', which basically means it won at least ten per cent of the vote at the last works council elections.

def: An employer's acceptance, voluntary or imposed by law, that it will negotiate with a particular union on behalf of a group of workers.

formal.ex: The union has made a formal request for [[recognition for collective bargaining purposes]].
formal.ex_us: The union has made a formal demand for [[recognition as bargaining representative]].

everyday.ex: The company finally agreed to [[recognise the union]] rather than fight it out.
everyday.ex_us: The company finally agreed to [[recognize the union]] rather than fight it out.

note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, l'employeur n'est tenu de négocier qu'avec un syndicat « recognised », volontairement ou à l'issue d'une procédure légale devant le Central Arbitration Committee. Cette étape n'existe pas en France, où la représentativité découle des élections.

def: The group of employees that a union represents and for whom it negotiates with the employer.

formal.ex: The agreement applies to all employees in the [[bargaining unit]], whether or not they are union members.

everyday.ex: Team leaders aren't in the [[bargaining unit]], so the pay deal doesn't cover them.
everyday.ex_us: Supervisors aren't in [[the unit]], so the contract doesn't cover them.

collocations: to be excluded from the unit
note_fr: Notion centrale aux États-Unis et au Royaume-Uni, sans équivalent en France, où l'accord s'applique à toute l'entreprise ou à toute la branche. Aux États-Unis, « the contract » désigne souvent la convention collective elle-même.

fr: NLRB (agence fédérale américaine des relations du travail)
def: The US federal agency that supervises union elections and deals with unfair labor practices in the private sector.

formal.ex: The union filed a charge with the [[National Labor Relations Board]] alleging that the employer had refused to bargain.

everyday.ex: If we get this wrong, we could end up in front of [[the NLRB]].

collocations: to file a charge with the NLRB
note_fr: Orthographe américaine obligatoire (« Labor »), même dans un texte britannique : c'est un nom propre. Au Royaume-Uni, les rôles voisins se répartissent entre le Central Arbitration Committee (reconnaissance syndicale) et Acas (conciliation).

def: A US state law under which employees cannot be forced to join a union or pay union fees in order to keep their job.

formal.ex: Under a state [[right-to-work law]], employees cannot be required to join a union or pay union fees as a condition of employment.

everyday.ex: Texas is a [[right-to-work state]], so nobody can be made to pay dues.

note_fr: Double faux ami. Ce n'est pas le « droit au travail » ; et au Royaume-Uni, « right to work » désigne l'autorisation de travailler sur le territoire (« right-to-work check »). Aux États-Unis, ces lois d'État interdisent de subordonner l'emploi à l'adhésion ou au paiement de cotisations syndicales.

fr: pratique déloyale en matière de relations du travail (États-Unis)
def: In US law, conduct by an employer or a union that is prohibited because it interferes with employees' collective rights.

formal.ex: Threatening employees with plant closure if they vote for a union constitutes an [[unfair labor practice]].

everyday.ex: The union has filed a [[ULP]] charge over the way the layoffs were announced.

collocations: to file an unfair labor practice charge
to commit an unfair labor practice
note_fr: Notion américaine (refus de négocier, représailles, ingérence), sans caractère pénal, à la différence du délit d'entrave. Gardez l'orthographe « labor ». Ne confondez pas avec « unfair dismissal », notion britannique de licenciement abusif.

def: The right of workers to form and join unions of their choice, and not to join one.

formal.ex: The Company recognises the principle of [[freedom of association]] and the right to collective bargaining.
formal.ex_us: The Company recognizes the principle of [[freedom of association]] and the right to collective bargaining.

everyday.uk: the right to join a union
everyday.us: the right to join a union
everyday.ex: People have [[the right to join a union]], and equally the right not to.

note_fr: « Syndical freedom » et « syndical liberty » sont des calques. « Freedom of association » est l'expression des conventions de l'OIT (en anglais « ILO ») ; aux États-Unis, on parle aussi de « the right to organize ».

def: Treating a person less well in pay, promotion or discipline because of union membership or activity.

formal.ex: Any decision on pay or promotion based on union membership constitutes [[anti-union discrimination]].

everyday.ex: He says his missed promotion is [[victimisation]], and we need to show it isn't.
everyday.ex_us: He says his missed promotion is [[retaliation]], and we need to show it isn't.

informal.ex: The unions are calling the reorganisation [[union busting]], plain and simple.
informal.ex_us: The unions are calling the reorganization [[union busting]], plain and simple.

collocations: to be passed over for promotion
detriment on grounds of union membership
note_fr: « Syndical discrimination » est un calque. « Union busting » est polémique : il désigne les manœuvres visant à empêcher ou à casser l'implantation syndicale ; ne l'employez jamais pour décrire votre propre client.

def: Trade unions and employers' organisations, seen as the two sides that negotiate employment matters together.

formal.ex: The reform was preceded by a national agreement between the [[social partners]].

everyday.ex: It's up to [[unions and employers]] to work out the details.

note_fr: « Social partners » appartient au vocabulaire européen : compris des spécialistes, il déroute un Américain. À l'oral, dites « unions and employers », « both sides of industry » (UK) ou « management and labor » (US).

def: Discussion, consultation and negotiation between an employer and the representatives of its employees.

formal.ex: The agreement aims to strengthen [[social dialogue]] at company level.

everyday.ex: There's been no real [[dialogue with the unions]] since the last restructuring.

note_fr: « Social » renvoie en anglais à la vie en société ou aux loisirs (« social event », « social media ») : hors contexte européen, « social dialogue » reste opaque. Équivalents naturels : « employee relations » (UK), « labor-management relations » (US).

def: The relationship between an employer and its workforce as a group, especially through unions and representatives.

formal.ex: She has twenty years' experience of [[industrial relations]] in the transport sector.
formal.ex_us: She has twenty years of experience in [[labor relations]] in the transportation sector.

everyday.ex: He heads up [[employee relations]] for the French sites.

note_fr: « Social relations » = relations entre personnes dans la société. Directeur des relations sociales : « Head of Employee Relations » (UK), « Director of Labor Relations » (US). Climat social : « employee relations climate » ou « workplace climate ».

def: The general state of relations between management, employees and their representatives at a given time.

formal.ex: The [[employee relations climate]] at the Lyon site has deteriorated markedly since the announcement.
formal.ex_us: The [[labor relations climate]] at the Lyon site has deteriorated markedly since the announcement.

everyday.uk: the mood on the shop floor
everyday.ex: [[The mood on the shop floor]] is pretty sour at the moment.
everyday.ex_us: [[The mood on the floor]] is pretty sour right now.

note_fr: « Social climate » est un calque que seuls les habitués de l'Europe continentale décodent. Baromètre social : « employee engagement survey » ou « pulse survey ». Un climat tendu : « tense » ou « strained », pas « tended ».

def: To make a relationship reliable again after it has been damaged.

formal.ex: Management's priority is to [[restore trust]] with employee representatives after the events of last spring.

everyday.ex: It'll take more than one good meeting to [[rebuild trust]] with the reps.

informal.ex: She spent her first six months [[mending fences]] with the unions.

note_fr: « Trust » = confiance dans une relation ; « confidence » = assurance, ou confiance dans une capacité (« confidence in the plan »). « To make confidence » est un calque. « To clear the air » : crever l'abcès, expression précieuse après un conflit.

def: Negotiation between employers and unions about pay and working conditions for a whole group of employees.

formal.ex: Pay scales are determined by [[collective bargaining]] at industry level.

everyday.ex: [[Negotiations with the unions]] start next week.

note_fr: « Bargaining » est indénombrable : « a collective bargaining » est faux ; pour une négociation précise, dites « a round of talks » ou « negotiations ». « A bargain » seul = une bonne affaire.

def: To discuss something with another party in order to reach an agreement.

formal.ex: The parties agree to [[enter into negotiations]] on working time within three months of signature.

everyday.ex: We're [[negotiating]] with three unions, and they don't all want the same thing.

informal.ex: It took two all-night sessions to [[hammer out]] a deal on shift pay.

collocations: to negotiate with the unions on pay
to sit down with the unions
to return to the negotiating table
note_fr: On négocie « with » quelqu'un, « on » ou « over » un sujet ; transitif pour le résultat (« to negotiate an agreement »). « To bargain » survit surtout dans « to bargain collectively » et « to bargain in good faith ». « To discuss about » est fautif.

def: A collective agreement negotiated between one employer and the unions represented in that company.

formal.ex: Working time is governed by a [[company-level agreement]] signed with the representative unions.

everyday.ex: Our [[company agreement]] is more generous than the industry one on parental leave.

note_fr: « Enterprise agreement » se comprend (c'est le terme australien), mais « company agreement » est plus naturel. « Accord » est réservé en anglais aux traités et à la diplomatie. Aux États-Unis, on dit « collective bargaining agreement » ou simplement « the union contract ».

def: A collective agreement negotiated between employers' organisations and unions for a whole sector of the economy.

formal.ex: On minimum pay rates, the [[industry-level agreement]] in principle prevails over the company agreement.

everyday.ex: Check the [[sector agreement]] first: it sets the minimum for each grade.
everyday.ex_us: Check the [[industry agreement]] first: it sets the minimum for each grade.

collocations: to fall within the scope of an agreement
note_fr: « Branch » = agence, succursale ou section syndicale, jamais un secteur d'activité : « branch agreement » est un contresens. La négociation de branche est marginale au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis, où l'on négocie entreprise par entreprise.

explain.written: An industry-level agreement (accord de branche) is a collective agreement concluded between employers' organisations and trade unions for an entire sector, which sets minimum standards for every company within its scope.
explain.spoken: In France, unions and employers negotiate for a whole industry, and that agreement sets a floor - minimum pay, job grades and so on - for every company in the sector.

def: A government decision that makes an industry-level agreement binding on all employers in the sector, including those that did not sign it.

formal.ex: Following the [[extension order]], the agreement binds every employer in the sector, including those that are not members of a signatory organisation.
formal.ex_us: Following the [[extension order]], the agreement binds every employer in the sector, including those that are not members of a signatory organization.

everyday.ex: Once the ministry [[extends the agreement]], it applies to us whether we like it or not.

collocations: to be binding on all employers in the sector
note_fr: « Extension » évoque d'abord une prolongation dans le temps : précisez « extension to all employers in the sector ». C'est ce mécanisme qui explique la couverture conventionnelle très élevée en France malgré une faible syndicalisation.

explain.written: By an extension order, the French Minister of Labour may make an industry-level agreement binding on all employers in the sector concerned, whether or not they belong to a signatory employers' organisation.
explain.spoken: Once the government 'extends' an industry agreement, every company in the sector has to apply it, even if it never signed anything.

def: The negotiations on pay and other set topics that a French employer with union delegates must open at regular intervals.

formal.ex: The [[mandatory annual negotiations]] on pay, working time and the sharing of added value opened on 12 January.
formal.ex_us: The [[mandatory annual negotiations]] on pay, working time and the sharing of added value opened on January 12.

everyday.ex: The [[annual pay talks]] start in January, so we need the budget signed off before Christmas.

note_fr: L'obligation porte sur l'ouverture de négociations loyales, non sur la conclusion d'un accord : « a duty to negotiate, not a duty to agree ». En cas d'échec, on dresse un procès-verbal de désaccord (« a record of disagreement »). « Mandatory » est plus naturel qu'« obligatory ».

explain.written: In French companies where representative unions are present, the employer is required to open negotiations at regular intervals, annually by default, on pay, working time and certain other matters; this is an obligation to negotiate in good faith, not to reach agreement.
explain.spoken: Every year we have to sit down with the unions and negotiate on pay and a few other topics. We don't have to reach a deal, but we do have to negotiate seriously.

fr: accord de dialogue social (fonctionnement du CSE)
def: A company agreement that organises employee representation: number of bodies, meetings, resources and consultation arrangements.

formal.ex: The [[agreement on social dialogue]] fixes the number of meetings, the content of the database and the time limits for consultation.

everyday.ex: Under our [[works council agreement]], each site council meets every two months and the central council once a quarter.

collocations: to adapt the statutory rules by agreement
note_fr: Dites à votre siège qu'en France une grande partie des règles du jeu (calendrier, délais, moyens) se négocie : « most of the ground rules can be tailored by agreement ». Équivalent le plus proche au Royaume-Uni : « recognition and procedure agreement ».

explain.written: The social dialogue agreement is a company-level collective agreement which tailors the statutory framework for employee representation, in particular the number and scope of works councils, the frequency of meetings, the resources of representatives and the arrangements for consultation.
explain.spoken: It's the agreement where we and the unions set the house rules for representation: how many councils, how often they meet, how much time and budget the reps get.

def: An agreement, signed before a negotiation or a major consultation, on how the process itself will be run.

formal.ex: Before opening talks on working time, the parties signed a [[method agreement]] setting out the timetable, the information to be shared and the resources allocated to the unions.

everyday.ex: Let's agree the [[ground rules]] first: how many meetings, what data, and who's in the room.
everyday.ex_us: Let's agree on the [[ground rules]] first: how many meetings, what data, and who's in the room.

note_fr: « Method agreement » demande une glose ; « ground rules » est l'expression naturelle, et même le terme consacré aux États-Unis pour le cadrage d'une négociation collective. On y recourt aussi pour encadrer la consultation lors des grandes restructurations.

explain.written: A method agreement (accord de méthode) is concluded between the employer and the unions ahead of a negotiation or a major consultation in order to fix the timetable, the information to be provided and the resources made available to the negotiators.
explain.spoken: Before we get into the substance, we sign a short agreement on the process: the calendar, the documents we'll share and the time the unions get to prepare.

def: To arrive at terms that both sides accept after negotiating.

formal.ex: The parties [[concluded an agreement]] on remote working on 3 June.
formal.ex_us: The parties [[concluded an agreement]] on remote working on June 3.

everyday.ex: We [[reached an agreement]] with two of the three unions late last night.

informal.ex: They finally [[struck a deal]] at four in the morning.

note_fr: « To conclude » seul signifie le plus souvent « terminer » ou « déduire » : réservez-le à l'écrit formel, suivi de « an agreement ». « To find an agreement » est un calque : dites « reach » ou « come to ».

def: In France, a company agreement signed by unions that together won more than half of the votes cast for representative unions.

formal.ex: To be valid, a company agreement must be a [[majority agreement]], signed by unions that won more than half of the votes cast for representative unions.

everyday.ex: Without the largest union on board it can't be a [[majority agreement]], so we'd need an employee vote.

collocations: to put the agreement to an employee vote
note_fr: Expliquez que le poids de chaque syndicat se mesure aux voix obtenues aux élections, non au nombre d'adhérents. Un accord signé par des syndicats représentant plus de 30 % peut encore être validé par un vote des salariés.

explain.written: Under French law a company agreement is valid only if it is signed by representative unions which together obtained more than fifty per cent of the votes cast for such unions at the last workplace elections, or, failing that, if it is approved by a majority of employees in a ballot.
explain.spoken: An agreement only stands if the unions signing it won more than half the union vote at the last elections - otherwise it has to go to a staff vote.

def: To give formal notice that one no longer intends to be bound by a collective agreement.

formal.uk: to give notice of termination of the agreement
formal.us: to give notice of termination of the agreement
formal.ex: Either signatory may [[give notice of termination of the agreement]], subject to the notice period for which it provides.

everyday.uk: to pull out of the agreement
everyday.us: to pull out of the agreement
everyday.ex: Management is threatening to [[pull out of the agreement]] on working time if the talks go nowhere.

collocations: to remain in force for a transitional period
note_fr: Faux ami majeur : « to denounce » = condamner publiquement ou dénoncer quelqu'un. Pour un accord : « terminate », « give notice to terminate », « withdraw from ». Après dénonciation, l'accord survit un temps : « it remains in force for a transitional period ».

def: To discuss an existing agreement again in order to change some of its terms.

formal.ex: The parties may [[revise the agreement]] by means of an amending agreement concluded under the same majority rules.

everyday.ex: The unions want to [[reopen the agreement]] now that inflation has picked up.

note_fr: En anglais britannique, « to revise » signifie aussi « réviser ses examens » ; en contexte juridique, il veut bien dire « modifier ». Avenant de révision : « amending agreement ». Clause de revoyure : « review clause » (US : « reopener clause »).

def: The things that employees or their unions firmly ask the employer to grant.

formal.ex: The unions submitted their [[demands]] in writing ahead of the first meeting.

everyday.ex: The [[pay claim]] this year is five per cent across the board.
everyday.ex_us: The [[wage demands]] this year are five percent across the board.

informal.ex: That's their [[wish list]]; what they'll settle for is another matter.

collocations: to put in a pay claim
note_fr: « Demand » est beaucoup plus fort que « demande » (= « request ») : il rend donc bien « revendication ». « Claim » au sens de revendication salariale est britannique ; aux États-Unis, il évoque plutôt une réclamation en justice.

def: An offer made in reply to an offer from the other side that one does not accept as it stands.

formal.ex: Management tabled a [[counter-proposal]] providing for a general increase of two per cent and a one-off bonus.
formal.ex_us: Management presented a [[counterproposal]] providing for a general increase of two percent and a one-time bonus.

everyday.ex: They turned down our [[counter-offer]] within the hour.
everyday.ex_us: They turned down our [[counteroffer]] within the hour.

collocations: to put an offer on the table
to come back with a counter-offer
note_fr: Piège célèbre : « to table a proposal » signifie la présenter au Royaume-Uni, mais la reporter sine die aux États-Unis. Avec des Américains, dites « to put forward » ou « to present ».

def: The agreement on pay increases that brings a round of pay negotiations to an end.

formal.ex: The [[pay settlement]] provides for a three per cent increase backdated to 1 January.
formal.ex_us: The [[wage settlement]] provides for a three percent increase retroactive to January 1.

everyday.ex: The [[pay deal]] went down well on the shop floor.

note_fr: « Settlement » désigne ici l'accord qui clôt la négociation ; le même mot sert pour une transaction mettant fin à un litige. Augmentation générale : « across-the-board increase » ; « pay rise » (UK) mais « raise » (US).

def: To give up part of what one wanted so that an agreement becomes possible.

formal.ex: Both parties [[made concessions]] in order to reach a balanced agreement.

everyday.ex: They won't [[give ground]] on pay, but there may be room on working time.

informal.ex: Look, if you can move on the bonus, we'll [[meet you halfway]] on the on-call rate.

note_fr: Donnant-donnant : « give and take » ou « a trade-off », surtout pas « giving-giving ». « To concede a point » = céder sur un point. Attention à « to compromise », qui peut aussi vouloir dire « compromettre ».

def: A situation in which negotiations cannot move forward because neither side will change its position.

formal.ex: The negotiations ended in [[deadlock]], and a record of disagreement was drawn up.
formal.ex_us: The negotiations reached an [[impasse]], and a record of disagreement was drawn up.

everyday.ex: Talks [[broke down]] on Friday over the night-shift premium.

note_fr: « Blocking » ne s'emploie pas comme nom dans ce sens, et « blockade » = blocus. Aux États-Unis, « impasse » est aussi une notion juridique : une fois l'impasse atteinte de bonne foi, l'employeur peut, sous conditions, appliquer sa dernière offre.

def: To find a way of getting blocked negotiations moving again.

formal.ex: A mediator was appointed in an attempt to [[break the deadlock]].
formal.ex_us: A mediator was appointed in an attempt to [[break the impasse]].

everyday.ex: A small gesture on the bonus might [[get talks moving again]].

collocations: to bring both sides back to the table
note_fr: « To unblock the situation » est un calque fréquent. Pensez à « a breakthrough » (une avancée décisive) et à « to find a way forward », très employés par les négociateurs.

fr: négocier de bonne foi (loyauté de la négociation)
def: To negotiate honestly, with a genuine intention of reaching an agreement.

formal.ex: The employer is under a duty to [[negotiate in good faith]] and to provide the unions with the information they need.

everyday.ex: Turning up with a final offer on day one isn't [[bargaining in good faith]].

note_fr: « Loyal » signifie « fidèle » : « loyal negotiation » est un contresens ; la loyauté se rend par « good faith » ou « fair dealing ». Aux États-Unis, manquer au « duty to bargain in good faith » constitue une « unfair labor practice ».

fr: soumettre l'accord au vote des adhérents
def: A vote in which union members decide whether to accept the agreement their negotiators have reached.

formal.uk: to put the agreement to a ballot of members
formal.us: to submit the agreement for ratification
formal.ex: The union will [[put the agreement to a ballot of members]] before signing.
formal.ex_us: The union will [[submit the agreement for ratification]] before signing.

everyday.us: to put it to a vote
everyday.ex: They're [[balloting members]] on the offer next week, with a recommendation to accept.
everyday.ex_us: They're [[putting it to a vote]] next week, with a recommendation to accept.

collocations: to vote to accept / reject the offer
note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis, le syndicat fait presque toujours valider le projet par ses adhérents. En France, le vote des salariés (« employee referendum ») n'intervient que dans des cas précis, par exemple pour valider un accord minoritaire. « To ballot » est transitif.

def: The rule that, where two sources of employment law conflict, the one more beneficial to the employee applies.

formal.ex: Under the [[favourability principle]], where two provisions conflict, the one more beneficial to the employee applies.
formal.ex_us: Under the [[favorability principle]], where two provisions conflict, the one more beneficial to the employee applies.

everyday.uk: whichever is better for the employee
everyday.us: whichever is better for the employee
everyday.ex: The old rule of thumb was [[whichever is better for the employee]], but company agreements now take priority on most topics.

note_fr: Notion à manier avec prudence : depuis les réformes de 2016 et 2017, l'accord d'entreprise prime dans la plupart des domaines, même moins favorable, sauf dans les matières réservées à la branche. « Favour principle » est un calque.

explain.written: The favourability principle (principe de faveur) is the traditional rule of French employment law under which, where several provisions apply to the same situation, the employee benefits from the most favourable one; its scope has been considerably reduced as regards the relationship between industry-level and company agreements.
explain.spoken: Traditionally, if two rules clashed, the employee got the better one. That's still true between the contract and an agreement, but much less so between industry and company agreements.

def: To set a rule that differs from a higher or more general rule, where the law allows it.

formal.ex: A company agreement may [[derogate from]] the industry-level agreement except in the areas reserved to the latter.

everyday.ex: On overtime rates you can [[depart from]] the sector agreement, within limits.
everyday.ex_us: On overtime rates you can [[depart from]] the industry agreement, within limits.

note_fr: « To derogate from » est juridique et correct mais rare à l'oral : préférez « to depart from » ou « to opt out of ». « Derogatory » signifie « désobligeant » : rien à voir. « À titre dérogatoire » : « by way of exception ».

def: In the UK, the employer's legal duty to consult employee representatives before large-scale redundancies or a business transfer.

formal.ex: Where twenty or more redundancies are proposed at one establishment within ninety days, the employer must carry out [[collective consultation]] with appropriate representatives.

everyday.ex: We'll have to [[consult collectively]] before any notices go out.

collocations: with a view to reaching agreement
note_fr: Notion britannique : faute de CSE, l'employeur qui envisage des licenciements collectifs consulte le syndicat reconnu ou, à défaut, des représentants élus pour l'occasion. Aux États-Unis, la loi n'impose qu'un préavis (« WARN notice »), sans consultation.

def: A period during which employees collectively stop working in support of their demands.

formal.ex: [[Strike action]] suspends the employment contract but does not terminate it.
formal.ex_us: A [[strike]] suspends the employment contract but does not terminate it.

everyday.ex: The drivers [[went on strike]] on Monday and nothing has left the depot since.

informal.ex: If the bonus is scrapped, they'll [[walk out]].

note_fr: « To make a strike » et « to do strike » sont fautifs : dites « to go on strike » ou « to strike ». « Strike action » est britannique. En France, la grève est un droit individuel de valeur constitutionnelle ; au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis, elle est avant tout l'affaire du syndicat.

def: For a union, to announce officially that its members should stop work.

formal.ex: Three unions have [[called a strike]] for 5 December in protest at the proposed closure.
formal.ex_us: Three unions have [[called a strike]] for December 5 to protest the proposed closure.

everyday.ex: The union's [[calling members out]] for 24 hours on Thursday.
everyday.ex_us: The union's [[calling a strike]] for 24 hours on Thursday.

note_fr: « To call for a strike » = appeler de ses vœux une grève ; « to call a strike » = la déclencher. Lever le mot d'ordre : « to call off the strike ». « Mot d'ordre » se rend par « strike call ».

def: Any collective action by employees, such as a strike or an overtime ban, intended to put pressure on the employer.

formal.ex: The union has given notice of [[industrial action]] short of a strike, including an overtime ban.
formal.ex_us: The union has announced a [[job action]] short of a strike, including a refusal of voluntary overtime.

everyday.ex: If there's [[industrial action]] in December, we'll miss the Christmas orders.
everyday.ex_us: If there's a [[job action]] in December, we'll miss the holiday orders.

note_fr: « Social movement » désigne un mouvement de société (droits civiques, écologie), jamais une grève. « Industrial » ne renvoie pas à l'industrie mais au monde du travail (« industrial relations », « industrial dispute »).

def: A disagreement between an employer and a group of employees or their union, typically about pay or conditions.

formal.ex: The parties shall refer any [[trade dispute]] to conciliation before taking industrial action.
formal.ex_us: The parties shall refer any [[labor dispute]] to mediation before resorting to a strike or lockout.

everyday.ex: The [[dispute]] over rosters has been dragging on for months.
everyday.ex_us: The [[dispute]] over schedules has been dragging on for months.

note_fr: « Social conflict » évoque des tensions dans la société, pas un conflit du travail. « Conflict » est possible mais plus général ; « dispute » est le terme technique. On est « in dispute with » son employeur.

def: The legal right of employees to stop work collectively in support of work-related demands.

formal.ex: The [[right to strike]] is guaranteed by the French Constitution and is exercised within the framework of the laws that govern it.

everyday.ex: Nobody's questioning their [[right to strike]]; the issue is the blockade of the warehouse.

collocations: to exercise the right to strike
note_fr: « Right of strike » est un calque. En France, un gréviste ne peut être licencié sauf faute lourde ; au Royaume-Uni, la protection suppose une action « protected » (vote régulier, préavis) ; aux États-Unis, les grévistes « économiques » peuvent être remplacés définitivement.

def: Formal advance warning given to an employer that a strike will begin on a certain date.

formal.ex: In the public services, a union must give five clear days' [[notice of strike action]].
formal.ex_us: In the public services, a union must give five clear days' [[strike notice]].

everyday.ex: They've served [[strike notice]] for the 14th, so we've got a week to find a way out.
everyday.ex_us: They've served [[strike notice]] for the 14th, so we have a week to find a way out.

note_fr: Dans le secteur privé français, aucun préavis n'est exigé : la grève peut démarrer dès que l'employeur connaît les revendications. Au Royaume-Uni, à l'inverse, le syndicat doit notifier l'employeur avant le vote, puis avant l'action. « Preadvice » n'existe pas.

def: A vote among union members on whether to go on strike.

formal.ex: A [[ballot for industrial action]] must be conducted by post and scrutinised independently.
formal.ex_us: A [[strike authorization vote]] gives union leaders the power to call a strike if talks fail.

everyday.ex: The [[strike ballot]] closes on Friday, and both sides expect a yes.
everyday.ex_us: The [[strike vote]] closes on Friday, and both sides expect a yes.

collocations: to vote in favour of strike action
note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, sans vote régulier, l'action n'est pas protégée ; aux États-Unis, le vote relève des statuts du syndicat. En France, aucun vote n'est requis : la grève est un droit individuel exercé collectivement.

def: A sudden, usually short, stoppage in which employees leave their work as a protest.

formal.ex: A two-hour [[work stoppage]] was observed on the morning shift.

everyday.ex: There was a [[walkout]] on line three this morning after the announcement.

informal.ex: They [[downed tools]] at ten and didn't come back till after lunch.
informal.ex_us: They [[walked off the job]] at ten and didn't come back until after lunch.

note_fr: « To walk out » (verbe), « a walkout » (nom, en un mot). « Débrayer » n'a rien à voir avec « to declutch ». « To down tools » est britannique et imagé ; il s'emploie même pour des employés de bureau.

def: A form of protest in which employees follow every rule and instruction so strictly that work slows down.

formal.ex: The union instructed its members to begin a [[work-to-rule]] from Monday.

everyday.ex: They're [[working to rule]], so every safety check takes twice as long.

note_fr: « Strike of zeal » ferait sourire. L'idée : appliquer chaque consigne à la lettre pour ralentir l'activité. Variantes : « to work to contract » (s'en tenir strictement au contrat) et « to withdraw goodwill » (cesser tout effort volontaire).

def: A group of strikers standing at the entrance to a workplace to publicise the strike and discourage others from going in.

formal.ex: Peaceful [[picketing]] is lawful, provided that it does not prevent non-strikers from entering the premises.

everyday.ex: There's a [[picket line]] at the main gate, but lorries are getting through.
everyday.ex_us: There's a [[picket line]] at the main gate, but trucks are getting through.

note_fr: « To picket » = tenir un piquet ; « a picket » désigne le groupe ou la personne. « To cross the picket line » est lourd de sens moral dans la culture syndicale anglo-saxonne. En France, le piquet devient illicite s'il porte atteinte à la liberté du travail des non-grévistes.

def: A person who works during a strike, or who is brought in to do the work of someone on strike.

formal.ex: French law prohibits the use of fixed-term or agency staff as [[replacement workers]] during a strike.

everyday.ex: Bringing in [[strike-breakers]] would poison relations for years.
everyday.ex_us: Bringing in [[strikebreakers]] would poison relations for years.

informal.ex: Anyone who went in that day was called a [[scab]] for months afterwards.

note_fr: « Scab » est une insulte : à comprendre, jamais à employer. Non-gréviste : « non-striker », terme neutre. Aux États-Unis, l'employeur peut sous conditions embaucher des « permanent replacements » pendant une grève économique, ce que le droit français interdit.

def: The closing of a workplace by the employer, who refuses to let employees work until a dispute is settled.

formal.ex: A [[lockout]] is in principle unlawful in France, save where the employer can show an overriding necessity.

everyday.ex: Management [[locked out]] the night shift after the damage to line two.

note_fr: En un seul mot en anglais ; le verbe est « to lock out ». Aux États-Unis, le lock-out est une arme économique licite de l'employeur, symétrique de la grève ; en France, il n'est admis qu'exceptionnellement (situation contraignante, impératifs de sécurité).

def: A strike that employees start on their own, without the approval of their union.

formal.ex: Employees who take part in [[unofficial industrial action]] have no protection against dismissal.
formal.ex_us: Employees who take part in an [[unauthorized strike]] in breach of a no-strike clause may be disciplined.

everyday.ex: It was a [[wildcat strike]]: the union knew nothing about it until the line stopped.

note_fr: Grève déclenchée sans l'aval du syndicat. La notion a peu de portée dans le secteur privé français, où la grève n'a pas à être syndicale ; elle est décisive au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis. « Savage strike » serait un contresens (« savage » = féroce).

def: A strike by employees who are not themselves in dispute, in support of other workers who are.

formal.ex: [[Secondary action]] in support of workers employed by another employer is unlawful in the United Kingdom.
formal.ex_us: A [[sympathy strike]] in support of workers at another employer may be barred by a no-strike clause.

everyday.ex: The dockers came out on a [[sympathy strike]] for two days.
everyday.ex_us: The dockworkers went out on a [[sympathy strike]] for two days.

note_fr: « Sympathy » = solidarité, compassion, et non « sympathie » (faux ami). En France, la grève de solidarité est licite si elle se rattache à des revendications professionnelles qui intéressent aussi les grévistes ; au Royaume-Uni, la « secondary action » est interdite.

fr: retenue sur salaire pour fait de grève
def: To reduce an employee's pay to take account of time not worked.

formal.uk: to make a deduction from pay
formal.us: to make a deduction from pay
formal.ex: The employer may [[make a deduction from pay]] strictly proportionate to the duration of the stoppage.

everyday.ex: We'll [[dock pay]] for the two hours, no more, no less.

note_fr: « Strike pay » est l'indemnité versée par le syndicat à ses adhérents grévistes, non le salaire dû par l'employeur. En France, la retenue doit être strictement proportionnelle à l'arrêt de travail ; au-delà, c'est une sanction pécuniaire interdite.

def: The moment when employees start working again after a strike.

formal.ex: The agreement provides for a [[return to work]] on Monday 9 June.
formal.ex_us: The agreement provides for a [[return to work]] on Monday, June 9.

everyday.ex: Most of the drivers [[went back to work]] this morning.

collocations: to vote to return to work
note_fr: « Resumption of work » est correct mais administratif. « Return to work » désigne aussi le retour après un arrêt maladie (« return-to-work interview ») : le contexte tranche. « Reprise » en anglais est un terme musical.

def: The agreement between management and unions that sets the terms on which a strike ends.

formal.ex: The [[agreement to end the dispute]] provides that no disciplinary action will be taken against the strikers.

everyday.ex: The unions won't sign a [[return-to-work agreement]] unless the strike days are spread over three months' pay.

collocations: to draw a line under the dispute
note_fr: « Protocol » ne convient pas (étiquette, procédure technique) : dites « agreement » ou « settlement ». La clause par laquelle l'employeur renonce aux sanctions s'appelle « no-victimisation clause » (UK) ou « no-reprisal clause » (US).

def: A process in which a neutral person helps the two sides in a dispute to find their own solution.

formal.ex: The parties agreed to refer the dispute to [[mediation]] before an independent third party.

everyday.ex: It might be worth [[bringing in a mediator]] before positions harden any further.

note_fr: Le médiateur propose, il ne tranche pas : « the mediator has no power to impose a solution ». Ne confondez pas avec « arbitration ». Aux États-Unis, un service fédéral de médiation intervient dans les négociations collectives.

def: A process in which a third party brings the two sides of a dispute together and helps them to settle it.

formal.ex: Before any industrial action, the dispute shall be referred to [[conciliation]].
formal.ex_us: Before any strike or lockout, the dispute shall be referred to [[conciliation]].

everyday.us: to call in a federal mediator
everyday.ex: Both sides have agreed to [[go to Acas]], which is a good sign.
everyday.ex_us: Both sides have agreed to [[call in a federal mediator]], which is a good sign.

note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, Acas est l'organisme public indépendant de conciliation, pour les conflits collectifs comme pour les litiges individuels ; « to go to Acas » est devenu une expression courante. Aux États-Unis, on parle presque toujours de « mediation ».

def: A process in which an independent person hears both sides of a dispute and makes a decision that they must accept.

formal.ex: Any dispute as to the interpretation of this agreement shall be settled by [[binding arbitration]].

everyday.ex: If we can't agree on the grading, it'll [[go to arbitration]].

collocations: to refer a dispute to arbitration
note_fr: L'arbitre (« arbitrator ») rend une décision qui s'impose aux parties (« award ») ; « arbitrage » est en anglais un terme de finance, et « referee » ou « umpire » sont réservés au sport. Très courant aux États-Unis pour les différends nés de la convention collective, rare en France en matière collective.

def: To bring a disagreement to an end by finding a solution both sides accept.

formal.ex: The joint committee was set up to [[resolve a dispute]] over the classification of maintenance staff.

everyday.ex: It took an outside mediator to [[settle a dispute]] that had dragged on since the spring.

informal.ex: Let's get everyone in a room and [[sort things out]] before it goes any further.
informal.ex_us: Let's get everyone in a room and [[work things out]] before it goes any further.

note_fr: « To regulate a conflict » est un calque (« regulate » = réglementer). « To solve » s'emploie pour un problème, « to resolve » ou « to settle » pour un différend ; « settle » implique souvent un compromis.

def: The ordinary members of a union, as opposed to its leaders and officials.

formal.ex: The leadership's recommendation was rejected by [[rank-and-file members]] in the ballot.
formal.ex_us: The leadership's recommendation was rejected by [[rank-and-file members]] in the ratification vote.

everyday.ex: The national officials are happy with the deal, but [[the rank and file]] aren't convinced.

collocations: to sell the deal to the members
note_fr: Image militaire (les rangs) : « the rank and file » désigne les adhérents de base, par opposition à la direction du syndicat ; verbe le plus souvent au pluriel. « The base » ne s'emploie pas dans ce sens, sauf en politique américaine.
